primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Autoimmune hepatitis is an immune-mediated inflammatory liver disease associated with loss of immune tolerance. Typical findings include hepatocellular aminotransferase elevation, increased IgG, autoantibodies such as ANA or anti-smooth-muscle antibody, and plasma-cell-rich interface hepatitis after competing causes are excluded.
vignette: A young woman has fatigue and jaundice. Serum aminotransferases are markedly elevated, serum IgG is increased, and testing is positive for antinuclear and anti-smooth-muscle antibodies. Viral hepatitis studies are negative. Liver biopsy shows portal plasma-cell-rich inflammation extending across the limiting plate into the periportal parenchyma.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractor_notes: Primary biliary cholangitis is a cholestatic small-duct disease classically associated with antimitochondrial antibodies rather than a plasma-cell-rich hepatocellular interface pattern.
Primary sclerosing cholangitis is a cholangiopathy characterized by multifocal biliary stricturing and is not defined by ANA/ASMA-associated interface hepatitis.
Wilson disease can cause hepatitis in young patients but requires evidence of abnormal copper metabolism and does not explain the characteristic autoimmune serology/IgG pattern.
Alcohol-associated hepatitis has a different exposure history and histologic pattern and does not explain the autoimmune markers and elevated IgG.
key_expl: The combination of hepatocellular injury, elevated IgG, ANA/anti-smooth-muscle antibodies, exclusion of viral hepatitis, and plasma-cell-rich interface hepatitis strongly supports autoimmune hepatitis. Interface hepatitis is the hallmark histologic pattern, although diagnosis integrates clinical, laboratory, serologic, and histologic findings.
objective: Recognize autoimmune hepatitis from elevated IgG, characteristic autoantibodies, hepatocellular injury, and plasma-cell-rich interface hepatitis.
